name: Kansas

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act of 2003, never amended (K.S.A. 44-1517 and following)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement deals, so NIL agents must register (K.S.A. 44-1517). Kansas has no NIL law of its own.
summary: Register with the Secretary of State by mail. $515, good for 2 years. You file a new application each time.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Registration Application
steps.detail: Include Appendices A to F: jobs, training, 3 references, athletes, owners and yes/no questions.
The law sets a $500 fee (K.S.A. 44-1524). The current form (rev. 1/29/26) asks for $515 for a paper filing.

steps.text: Mail it to the Secretary of State
steps.detail: Docking State Office Building, 915 SW Harrison St., Topeka, KS 66612. Online filing is not offered.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Warn the athlete before signing that the contract may make them ineligible
steps.detail: Kansas makes it a crime to skip this.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get for the deal, anyone not in your application who gets paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student-athlete next to their signature
steps.detail: Bold capital letters, right by the athlete's signature. Use the exact wording Kansas gives.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell the athletic director too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days if they want
steps.detail: They cancel by telling you in writing.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Kansas law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract, and what you spent to recruit each athlete. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes or make false promises
steps.detail: No false promises. No gifts or money to the athlete before signing, or to anyone else to get them. Don't contact athletes until you're registered. It's a class A misdemeanor.

steps.text: File a new application before 2 years are up
steps.detail: Kansas has no renewal. Registration ends 2 years after filing.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The statute fee is $500 but the form asks for $515. Ask the Secretary of State (785-296-4564) what the extra $15 covers.
The warning wording was read through a summary tool. Compare it word for word with K.S.A. 44-1525 before printing contracts.
